title: Zeta Valued at $2 Billion In New $50 Million Strategic Fundraise
summary: Zeta Valued at $2 Billion In $50 Million Strategic Fundraise. Pre-money valuation jumps 1.7x from $1.15B in prior round
body_text: Zeta Valued at $2 Billion In New $50 Million Strategic Fundraise Pre-money valuation jumps 1.7x from $1.15B in prior round San Ramon, February 11, 2025: Zeta, a next-gen banking tech provider to financial institutions globally, today announced it has secured a $50 million investment from a strategic investor valuing it at $2 billion. Zeta had previously been valued at a pre-money valuation of $1.15 billion when it raised $250 million from Softbank Vision Fund 2 and other marquee investors in 2021. “We are incredibly excited at the pace at which clients are embracing our modern stack,” said Zeta’s Global CEO and Co-founder, Bhavin Turakhia . He added, “Over the past few years, we have supported over 25 million accounts on our cloud-native processing platform Tachyon and are on track to add 25 million more with contracts already in flight. Our clients are breaking away from decades of legacy systems to deliver amazing digital experiences thereby increasing their customer satisfaction and accelerating new user acquisition.” Zeta’s SaaS offerings enable Banks and Fintechs to launch any asset, liability or payment product including credit cards, checking accounts, savings accounts, unsecured loans, and more – for consumers, SMBs and corporates on a modern, Microservices based, API-first, Cloud-native, and Headless (MACH) platform. Zeta’s SaaS suite encompasses every step of the customer lifecycle of a banking product, comprising the below offerings: Tachyon: Core Banking & Issuer Payments Suite Photon: Merchant Acquiring & Payments Service Provider Suite Neutrino: Digital Banking & AI Applications Suite Saturn: Issuer Operations & Servicing Suite Luminos: Customer Engagement & Rewards Suite Electron: Commercial Cards & Benefits Suite Quark: Data & Intelligent Applications Suite Commenting on the recent trajectory, Zeta’s Co-founder, Ramki Gaddipati said “Zeta’s mission to be a trusted partner to financial institutions is possible through the patient efforts of the best team ever assembled in banking technology. While the past few years have been challenging for the banking-tech industry, our organization has delivered multiple winning programs for our clients in record times. About Zeta Zeta is a next-gen banking technology company. Zeta’s platform enables financial institutions to launch extensible and compliant asset and liability products rapidly. Its cloud-native and fully API-enabled stack supports processing, issuing, lending, core banking, fraud, loyalty, digital banking apps, and many other capabilities. Zeta has 1700+ employees with over 70% in technology roles across locations in the US, Middle East, and Asia – representing one of the largest and most capable teams ever assembled in banking tech. Globally, customers have issued 25M+ cards on Zeta’s platform. Visit us at www.zeta.tech or follow us on LinkedIn , YouTube , and X For media queries, please contact: Rishav Kumar Manager, PR, and Analyst Relations [email protected]

title: Employee Records and Leave Management Software FAQs for Growing Companies
summary: Title Tag: Employee Records and Leave Management Software FAQs | Asure Meta Description: Answers to 22 common questions about HR employee file management, leave tracking, onboarding, and compliance software for growth-stage companies. From Asure.
body_text: Title Tag: Employee Records and Leave Management Software FAQs | Asure Meta Description: Answers to 22 common questions about HR employee file management, leave tracking, onboarding, and compliance software for growth-stage companies. From Asure. This hub answers 22 common questions about centralizing your employee records and leave workflows as your company scales. Organized into five sections, employee file and document management, leave and absence tracking, onboarding records, compliance and audit readiness, and software selection, these answers draw on HR operations expertise at Asure to help you replace spreadsheets and scattered file storage with a compliant, connected system. Employee File & Document Management Every growing company eventually outgrows paper folders and shared drives for storing employee information. These five questions cover what HR file management software actually does, how it differs from broader HR systems, and what compliance standards shape which documents belong where. What is HR employee file management software? HR employee file management software is a digital system that stores each employee's personnel file, from offer letters to performance reviews, in one secure, searchable record. It replaces paper folders and shared drives with structured storage and role-based access controls, so only authorized HR staff, managers, or auditors can view sensitive documents based on their permission level. What is the difference between an HRIS and HR document management software? An HRIS stores structured employee data, such as compensation, job history, and status changes, in defined fields that support reporting and payroll calculations. HR document management software instead stores unstructured files, contracts, signed policies, offer letters, and acknowledgment forms, tied to each employee's record. Growing companies often need both, which is why platforms that combine structured data and document storage in one system reduce duplicate entry. What documents should be stored in an employee personnel file? A general personnel file typically holds offer letters, signed policy acknowledgments, performance reviews, disciplinary notes, and pay or role change records. Form I-9, the federal Employment Eligibility Verification form, and medical or disability-related documents do not belong in that file. Under Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) , medical and disability-related information must be kept confidential in a separate file, and I-9 forms are commonly stored separately as well. What is document automation for human resources? Document automation for human resources refers to software that generates HR paperwork automatically by pulling employee data, such as name, title, pay rate, and start date, into pre-built templates. Instead of manually drafting each document, HR teams can auto-generate offer letters, non-disclosure agreements, and policy acknowledgment forms, then route them for electronic signature and filing into the employee's record. How does HR file management software improve compliance recordkeeping? HR file management software improves compliance recordkeeping by replacing manual, error-prone processes with structured storage, retention rules, and access logs. When personnel records live in scattered spreadsheets or paper files, missing signatures, misfiled I-9 forms, and expired retention periods are common findings when an audit or agency request occurs. Centralized software, such as AsureCentral, applies consistent retention and access rules across every employee file, regardless of who created it. Leave & Absence Tracking Leave requests, accrual tracking, and payroll deductions create some of the most error-prone manual work in growing HR teams. These five questions cover how leave management software works, how it differs from absence tracking, and what a growing, multi-state workforce needs from a leave system. What is leave management software? Leave management software is a system that automates how employees request time off and how employers track, approve, and calculate that time. Core capabilities include automated accrual calculations for PTO and sick time, routing leave requests to the right manager or HR contact, and structured approval workflows that create a record of who approved what and when. What is the difference between leave management and absence management software? Leave management software covers planned, policy-governed time off, such as PTO, vacation, and Family and Medical Leave Act, or FMLA, leave, where requests are submitted and approved in advance. Absence management software instead focuses on unplanned absences, such as unscheduled call-outs, and tracks attendance patterns over time. Growing companies often need both functions working from the same employee and schedule data. How does leave of absence management software handle FMLA compliance? Leave of absence management software handles FMLA compliance by tracking key deadlines and generating required notices automatically. Under the Department of Labor's FMLA regulations , once an employer has notice that a leave request may qualify, it generally must notify the employee of FMLA eligibility, which may be given orally or in writing, within five business days, followed by a written designation notice once the employer has enough information to make that determination. Software can flag these deadlines so HR does not miss them. Can leave management software integrate with payroll systems? Yes, leave management software commonly integrates with payroll through a bi-directional sync that passes approved leave hours directly into payroll as deductions or PTO draws, without manual re-entry. On a connected platform such as AsureCentral, leave requests, approvals, and payroll run from the same employee record, so an approved absence updates pay calculations automatically instead of requiring a separate spreadsheet reconciliation step. What should I look for in employee leave tracking software? Strong employee leave tracking software should offer flexible accrual configuration, since PTO, sick, and parental leave rules vary by state and employer policy. It should also support multi-state leave law differences, manager self-service, and audit trail logging that records every request, approval, and balance change. These four criteria matter because manual tracking breaks down first as headcount and states grow. Teams without payroll staff can have AsureWorks specialists manage this, with no co-employment and the client remaining employer of record. Onboarding Records & Workflows Onboarding is the first compliance-critical document event in an employee's file, and it is also where many growing companies still rely on manual paperwork. These four questions cover what onboarding software does, how it affects compliance and turnover, and how it connects back to the employee's ongoing personnel record. What is HR onboarding software? HR onboarding software is a system that manages the tasks and documents required to bring a new hire from offer acceptance to first day. Typical capabilities include digital Form I-9 completion, electronic signature for offer letters and policy acknowledgments, and automated task assignment that notifies IT, payroll, and facilities teams to provision equipment, set up pay, and prepare a workspace. How does onboarding software improve compliance for growing companies? Onboarding software improves compliance for growing companies by making sure every required document, from I-9 forms to policy acknowledgments and benefits elections, is collected, signed, and filed before or on a new hire's start date. Consistent, tracked onboarding also closes a gap that matters beyond compliance, since poor onboarding experiences are associated with higher first-year turnover, which creates its own recurring hiring and paperwork burden. What HR tasks can be automated during employee onboarding? Several onboarding tasks can be automated once a new hire accepts an offer. Common examples include document collection, such as I-9 and W-4 forms, benefits enrollment prompts sent at the right time, equipment provisioning tickets routed to IT, and policy acknowledgment tracking that confirms an employee has read and signed required handbooks and disclosures. How does onboarding software connect to employee file management? Onboarding software connects to employee file management by automatically filing completed documents into the employee's digital personnel record as soon as they are signed. Instead of an HR administrator downloading a signed offer letter or I-9 form and manually uploading it into a separate file system, the document lands directly in the right employee record, in the right file, on a connected platform such as AsureCentral, without a manual transfer step. HR Compliance & Audit Readiness Compliance risk in employee records is not abstract. Federal agencies set specific retention periods and documentation rules, and falling short of them is what turns a routine audit or agency inquiry into a real problem. These four questions cover the rules that matter most and how software helps meet them. How long are employers required to retain employee personnel files? Retention periods depend on the type of record. Under Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) recordkeeping rules , most personnel records must be kept for at least one year, extending to one year from the termination date for involuntary terminations. Payroll records must be kept for at least three years under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) , and Form I-9 must be retained for three years after hire or one year after termination, whichever is later. What is HR compliance SaaS? HR compliance SaaS is cloud-delivered software that helps employers meet regulatory and policy obligations without maintaining on-premise servers or manual tracking systems. It typically enforces policy workflows, such as requiring a signed acknowledgment before a policy takes effect, tracks regulatory deadlines like filing dates and leave notice windows, and generates audit-ready reports on demand rather than requiring HR staff to assemble them manually. How does HR software create an audit trail for employee records? HR software creates an audit trail through timestamped access logs that record who viewed, edited, or deleted a document, and exactly when that action occurred. Rather than relying on memory or email threads to reconstruct what happened to a file, HR and compliance teams can pull a complete history for any employee record, which matters directly during an agency audit or an internal investigation. What are the biggest compliance risks of managing HR records in spreadsheets? The biggest risks of managing HR records in spreadsheets are the controls a spreadsheet cannot enforce. There are no role-based access controls to limit who can view sensitive data, no version history to show what changed and when, no automatic retention enforcement, and no audit trail. A shared spreadsheet also makes it easy to violate ADA confidentiality rules by storing medical information alongside general personnel data instead of in a separate file. Software Selection & Integration Choosing software for employee records and leave management usually comes down to one tradeoff, breadth versus depth, plus how well a system fits a growing, multi-state workforce. The next four questions use scalability, configurability, integration, and security certification as evaluation criteria, since those are the dimensions that tend to break down first as a company grows past a single location. What is the difference between a point solution and a full HRIS for HR records and leave management? A point solution, such as a dedicated leave management tool, solves one workflow deeply but stores its data separately from the rest of the employee record. A full HRIS covers payroll, HR, and records in one place, though depth on specialized workflows like multi-state leave administration can vary by platform. AsureCentral combines HRIS breadth with dedicated leave and document management depth in one connected system. What is an employee database management system? An employee database management system is a structured repository that stores core employee data, including demographic information, compensation, job role, and employment status, in a searchable, centralized format. It typically includes role-based access so only authorized users see sensitive fields, along with reporting tools that let HR and finance teams pull headcount, turnover, or compensation data without manually compiling it from separate files. How do I evaluate HR workflow software for a growing company? Evaluate HR workflow software against four practical criteria. First, confirm it scales to 500 or more employees so you are not replatforming again in two years. Second, check for configurable approval chains that match your management structure. Third, confirm integration with your existing payroll and applicant tracking systems. Fourth, ask whether the vendor holds SOC 2 Type II certification, a System and Organization Controls audit of security and data-handling practices. What integrations should HR records and leave software have? HR records and leave software should integrate with your payroll system, whether that is ADP, Gusto, Paychex, or another provider, so approved hours and leave flow into pay runs without manual entry. It should also connect to your applicant tracking system, such as Greenhouse or Lever, for a clean handoff from candidate to employee record, plus benefits administration and single sign-on providers like Okta or Microsoft Entra ID for secure, centralized login. Learn More Centralizing your employee records and leave workflows is one of the highest-leverage operational decisions your HR team can make as headcount grows. The right software eliminates manual filing, enforces retention and access rules automatically, and gives you real-time visibility into headcount, leave balances, and document status. The resources below go deeper on each topic. When you are ready to see it in practice, AsureCentral brings records, leave, and compliance workflows into one connected system, and AsureWorks gives you the same system of record with Asure specialists managing the day-to-day work, with no co-employment and you remaining employer of record. title: How to Batch Your Email Replies Without Missing Urgent Messages
summary: Batch email replies smartly to save focus! Design urgency, filter quick, and set clear response windows for effective communication.
body_text: Why batching email replies works when you design for urgency Your inbox rewards interruptions. Your focus needs long stretches. Batching gives you those stretches without risking silence on urgent issues. Context switching costs time. Each jump to email taxes attention. Batching reduces jumps and protects deep work. Decide what is urgent. Design a path for these items. For all other messages, create a system to handle them based on their importance. Urgent messages bypass the queue. Routine messages land in scheduled batches. You control when you engage, not your inbox. Define what “urgent” actually means for your life and work Write a short rule set. Keep it simple and testable. Family or safety issues: respond within 15 minutes. Client delivery risks due today: respond within one hour. Payments, invoices, or access problems: respond within two hours. Everything else: reply during your next batch window. Share these rules with clients and collaborators. Clear rules remove guesswork and reduce “just checking in” emails. Build a fast pre‑filter so urgent messages surface instantly Use a few strong signals. Combine sender, keywords, and channels. Signals that work well Specific senders: your partner, key clients, or your executive’s address. Keywords that imply risk: “outage,” “blocked,” “contract today,” “wire,” “invoice due.” Phone numbers in the body, which often indicate real‑time needs. VIP lists on iOS or Priority Senders on Android for push alerts. Route those emails to one Urgent label or folder. Allow notifications only for that label. Mute everything else. Create two inboxes: urgent now and batched later You need one lane for “answer now,” and another for “answer at 1 pm.” Urgent now: messages from VIPs or matching urgent keywords. Batched later: newsletters, updates, routine requests, and FYIs. Consider an alias for emergencies, like you+urgent@ . Request top clients to use it only for critical matters that require immediate attention. Add a short rule: if a message is both urgent and unclear, call or text the sender for clarity before replying. Share clear response windows and set gentle expectations Setting clear expectations reduces unnecessary follow‑ups. Place a one‑line promise in your signature. I check email at 11 am and 4 pm. For urgent issues, please text me. Use a short auto‑reply during heavy weeks. Keep it friendly and precise. Thanks for your message. I reply in my next batch window today. If this is urgent, text my number with URGENT in the first word. The 30‑minute loop you can repeat all week Spend five minutes scanning the Urgent folder. Resolve or schedule follow‑ups. Spend twenty‑five minutes answering Batched Later. Work oldest to newest. Run this loop two or three times daily. Protect mornings for real work when possible. If a batch overruns, stop anyway. The limit keeps you honest and focused. Move work out of email into a workspace or CRM Email is a poor place to track deliverables. Turn threads into tasks, deals, or knowledge records the moment action appears. Convert a client thread into a task with a due date and owner. Attach the thread to the client’s CRM contact for context. Store final decisions where your team can find them later. All‑in‑one tools help here. Compare options before you commit. This guide can help you compare all‑in‑one workspaces with dedicated project tools . Tools like Routine and Notion compete in this space. Many freelancers also consider ClickUp for simple handoffs. Are you handling customer conversations through email, Intercom, or Front? Learn how to merge customer data from these platforms without coding and keep one clean timeline. Automations that cut noise but keep escalation alive Automate the easy sorting. Preserve at least one human path to you. Flag invoices and payment emails with a finance label and two‑hour SLA. Auto‑file newsletters into Read Later. Review them once a week. Forward bids or RFPs to your CRM. Assign an owner on arrival. Escalate no‑reply threads after 24 hours to SMS or a team chat. Whitelist your emergency alias so it always notifies on your phone. Keep rules short and transparent. Over‑automation hides real work. Exceptions to plan for before you start batching Some events deserve a manual override. Decide the trigger and the move. Legal or compliance requests: log the request, then respond promptly. Service outages: call first, email second. Document after recovery. New client kickoff week: temporarily add a midday quick check. Travel days: extend batch windows and tell key contacts the new plan. Write these exceptions down. Share them with partners and assistants. Track results and tune the system Measure outcomes, not feelings. Adjust rules based on data. First Response Time for Urgent: keep it under one hour. Average Time to Reply for Batched: set a day‑specific target. Batch Size: keep replies per batch steady to prevent overflow. Escalations: investigate each one and refine the trigger. If Urgent volume grows, tighten keywords or remove noisy senders. If batches become overwhelming, consider reducing newsletters, unsubscribing from irrelevant ones, or reassessing your filtering and sorting strategies. After two weeks, review the numbers. Keep what works. Retire the rest. FAQ How does batching email replies increase productivity? Batching reduces frequent context switching, allowing for focused, uninterrupted work periods. While urgent messages are prioritized, non-urgent ones wait for scheduled attention, reducing distraction and mental fatigue. Why is it important to define \"urgent\" in email management? Defining \"urgent\" helps to prioritize issues effectively and avoid the panic of constant interruptions. Without clear definitions, there is a risk of treating everything as urgent, which can spiral into chaos and decrease productivity. What’s the risk of not using a pre-filter for urgent emails? Without a pre-filter, crucial messages might get lost in a sea of routine emails, leading to missed deadlines or overlooked critical issues. A smart filtering system ensures immediate visibility for time-sensitive communication. How can setting response windows impact client relationships? Clearly communicated response times reduce client anxiety and the likelihood of follow-up emails. This control fosters stronger client trust, but failing to meet these expectations can quickly erode that trust. What are the potential drawbacks of over-automation in email management? Over-automation can create blind spots where genuinely urgent issues are ignored due to stringent rules. Maintaining a balance between automation and personal judgment is critical to ensure essential tasks are not inadvertently sidelined. Why should work be moved from email into a CRM or workspace? Email is an inefficient tool for tracking and managing tasks, which can lead to disorganization and missed deadlines. Converting emails into actionable items in a CRM or workspace like Routine helps maintain accountability and clarity. How should exceptions to batching rules be handled? Predefined exceptions should be documented and shared with teams to ensure swift responses during unusual circumstances. Failing to have exceptions can result in important tasks being delayed, especially in crisis situations. What should you do if batch sizes become overwhelming? If batch sizes grow unmanageable, it's crucial to reassess filtering strategies and reduce subscriptions or irrelevant content. Ignoring this can lead to burnout and inefficiencies, defeating the purpose of batching.

title: How Lean Tech Shrank Demo SLAs from One Week to One Hour
summary: Sep 19, 2025. Lean Technologies cut demo build time from a week to under an hour by replacing bespoke slides and mockups with interactive, reusable demos in Coast. The shift unified their end-to-end product story, freed sales from engineering, and lifted results - double-digit growth in data products and a 42% conversion jump on lending demos.
body_text: Lean Technologies provides open banking infrastructure for fintechs across the Middle East. Its platform enables A2A payments, account data access, and real-time financial experiences across a growing network of banks and startups. With over 260 clients and more than 500,000 end users, Lean is an open banking leader in MENA. The company has raised more than $100 million in funding—most recently a $67.5M Series B led by General Catalyst—and processes over $2.5 billion in payment volume. With Lean’s rapid growth, it became even more important to be able to clearly demonstrate their product capabilities: “Everyone has empathy for things they can see. As an API the ways our product can be used are varied and complex - the same data attribute can be used across multiple user journeys and processes. This creates an internal and external challenge when trying to showcase the value Lean can bring throughout a prospect's entire user journey from onboarding to payments.” — Alex, VP of Product Sales conversations grew longer and more complex. Without a front-end, Lean struggled to convey what its APIs could actually enable. Each demo was custom-built—requiring a full week of work across sales, product, design, and engineering. ‍ That changed with Coast. ‍ Today, Lean generates tailored, interactive demos in less than a day. Sales teams can showcase product capabilities visually, without relying on engineering. Instead of manually stitching together assets, teams share a single URL that tells a cohesive product story—one that’s easy to forward, reuse, and scale across enterprise buyers. ‍ Disjointed tools slowed growth ‍ Before Coast, Lean relied on Pitch, Figma, and custom-built sites to create 1:1 demos. The challenges were consistent: Time intensive : Custom demos took up to one week of cross-functional effort Engineering burden : Updates pulled dev teams off roadmap work Inconsistent messaging : Sellers told different stories depending on the asset Sales bottleneck : Product and solutions engineers had to join early-stage calls ‍ “Every demo felt like a one-off,” said Alex. “Even though our product is scalable, our story wasn’t.” From static storytelling to interactive selling Lean rebuilt its entire product narrative in Coast in under a week. The impact was immediate: Interactive demos became central to every sales pitch Sales teams operated independently on most deals Product only stepped in for strategic accounts For the first time, Lean could show the full end-to-end experience—onboarding, payments, insights, refunds—in a single, consistent interactive flow. Prototyping new use cases and unlocking revenue Coast also enabled rapid prototyping. When Lean identified a new use case for neobank onboarding, the team built the demo in Coast and pitched it within a month—before the product was fully live. The deal closed. Implementation is now underway. “The platform helps us go from idea to market faster than ever before,” Alex said. Quantifiable results Demo creation time dropped from 1 week to <1 hour Double-digit growth in data product sales over 6 months 42% higher conversion on lending demos End-to-end utility across teams Lean now uses Coast beyond sales—for onboarding, training, and field enablement: New hires ramp up by exploring real product flows, not static docs Field teams showcase products live at major conferences GTM teams prototype and test new narratives before launch ‍ “Everyone can finally see what our platform actually does,” said Alex. ‍

title: BankUnited Opens New Tampa Westshore Branch, Plans St. Petersburg Branch to Support Continued Growth in the Region
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about BankUnited, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: MIAMI LAKES, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 13, 2026-- BankUnited Inc. (NYSE: BKU) has announced the opening of a new, full-service branch in Westshore, Tampa, Florida, continuing the bank’s significant momentum in the region. It also announced plans to open a new St. Petersburg, Florida branch in the fourth quarter of this year. “Our new Westshore branch and the planned St. Petersburg branch will provide personal and commercial banking solutions to the professionals and businesses that make these communities thrive,” said Ernie Diaz, senior executive vice president, head of consumer, small business and commercial banking, BankUnited. “The Tampa region is experiencing strong growth across many industries and BankUnited is there to support customer needs and help bolster the regional economy.” The new branches come on the heels of BankUnited’s recent opening of a new downtown Tampa corporate office, fortifying its commercial and corporate banking services and CRE lending growth in the area. Kris-Eric Surillo, BankUnited market leader and vice president, was recently hired to oversee the new Westshore branch and the existing Tampa/Henderson branch location. Surillo, a 20-year bank professional, joins BankUnited from Synovus Bank in the Tampa region. He is a strong motivational leader known for developing and coaching exceptional teams. Named one of the World’s Most Trustworthy Companies by Newsweek magazine, Miami Lakes-based BankUnited is one of the largest independent depository institutions headquartered in Florida. The bank now operates in Florida, New York, Dallas, Atlanta, Morristown, New Jersey, and Charlotte, North Carolina. BankUnited provides a broad range of consumer and commercial banking products and services to individuals, small businesses, middle-market companies, large corporations and institutions. The nearly 3,500 sq. ft. location is at 1808 N Westshore Blvd., Tampa, FL 33607. It features ATM services and a night drop depository. For more information call 813-281-8500 or visit BankUnited.com . The St. Petersburg branch will be located at 900 Central Avenue, St. Peterburg, FL 33175. About BankUnited, N.A. BankUnited, Inc. (NYSE: BKU), with total assets of $35.4 billion at March 31, 2026, is the bank holding company of BankUnited, N.A., a national bank headquartered in Miami Lakes, Florida, with operations in Florida, New York, Dallas, Atlanta, Morristown, New Jersey, and Charlotte, North Carolina. BankUnited provides a full range of consumer and commercial banking products and services to individuals, small businesses, middle-market companies, large corporations and institutions, and offers certain commercial lending and deposit products through national platforms. For additional information, call (877) 779-2265 or visit www.BankUnited.com . BankUnited can be found on Facebook at facebook.com/BankUnited.official , LinkedIn @BankUnited and on X @BankUnited. title: AudioCodes Is an Approved Partner for Microsoft’s Operator Connect Accelerator
summary: AudioCodes announced it's approval as a partner for Microsoft’s Operator Connect Accelerator.
body_text: Lod, Israel – April 25, 2022 - AudioCodes (NASDAQ: AUDC) Press Release AudioCodes Live Cloud accelerates Operator Connect onboarding and operations for service providers AudioCodes, a leading vendor of advanced communications software, products and productivity solutions for the digital workplace, today announced that it has been approved as a partner for Microsoft’s Operator Connect Accelerator. AudioCodes can now offer service providers simplified customer onboarding and operation through the AudioCodes Live Cloud solution, enabling operators to sell voice services via the Microsoft Teams Operator Connect Marketplace. AudioCodes Live Cloud is a white label, multi-tenant SaaS solution that enables service providers to rapidly onboard their customers to Microsoft Teams voice services through either Microsoft Operator Connect or Direct Routing connectivity. It eliminates the certification and verification approval required from Microsoft third parties – including discovery, environment setup, preproduction testing, networking validation, final testing and approval for using the service provider’s brand – as well as meeting and exceeding Microsoft’s SLA and quality metrics standards. AudioCodes Live Cloud also empowers end customers with an advanced, self-service user policy management portal. Service providers can leverage AudioCodes Live Cloud to offer both Microsoft Operator Connect and Direct Routing connectivity to their customers, streamlining the process of connecting enterprise voice services to Microsoft Teams. This frees up operators to concentrate on their go-to-market activities, while reducing the total cost of ownership. AudioCodes Live Cloud is offered as a managed solution hosted in the service provider’s data center or public cloud, or as a pure SaaS solution, giving service providers high flexibility in their design choice. It includes AudioCodes’ market-leading session border controllers (SBCs), which are certified by Microsoft for Direct Routing and Operator Connect. “We are delighted to welcome AudioCodes as an Operator Connect Accelerator partner, helping service providers deliver enterprise-grade connectivity to their customers,” said Taimoor Husain, Global Strategy Lead for Operators at Microsoft. “Given the global growth in digital transformation, Operator Connect represents a genuine opportunity to simplify Microsoft Teams voice calling adoption and boost productivity” “AudioCodes Live Cloud is the ideal SaaS solution for assisting service providers to accelerate Operator Connect customer onboarding and operations, all on a per-user per-month plan,” added Lior Aldema, Chief Business Officer at AudioCodes. “Service providers can take full advantage of AudioCodes’ field-proven voice expertise to simplify Microsoft Teams voice connectivity, as well as offer Microsoft-certified business phones and meeting room devices .”

title: How to track client treatment without adding paralegal hours
summary: Treatment follow-up eats case-manager hours. See how Hona's AI Care Coordinator tracks appointments, gaps, and providers across every case without new headcount.
body_text: Ask a personal injury case manager where their week goes and the honest answer is follow-up. Confirming appointments. Texting the client who went quiet. Logging which provider someone saw last. It is essential work, and it scales in exactly the wrong direction. Every new case adds more of it, and the obvious fix is always more people. Why treatment tracking eats so many hours It never stops. While a client is treating, the reminders, confirmations, and check-ins keep coming. It is spread across every active case. A full caseload means dozens of clients at different points in care, each needing a nudge at a different time. It hides until it hurts. A client who quietly stopped treating six weeks ago is a problem you discover at the worst possible moment, when the demand is being built. Most firms keep up by adding hours: a longer task list for the case manager, or another paralegal once the caseload grows. That works until it does not, and it caps how many cases the firm can carry. Track treatment without growing the team There is another way to absorb the work, and it does not mean replacing the people who do it. Hona's AI Care Coordinator handles the routine treatment touchpoints a case manager would otherwise chase by hand, over text, across every active case. Checks in with clients through the treatment phase and keeps them moving. Confirms upcoming appointments and catches the ones that get missed. Tracks where each client is in care, including the providers they are seeing, so the picture stays current instead of being reconstructed later. Escalates to your team the moment something needs a human. The piece that makes this work is that it is interactive. A one-way reminder blast falls apart the second a client texts back, and a client who is actively treating will text back. The AI Care Coordinator can respond, follow up after an appointment, and pick up on a new provider the client mentions. Free your team for the work only people can do The aim is more capacity from the same team, not a smaller one. When the appointment reminders and check-ins run on their own, your case managers can spend their time on the conversations that need a human: the empathy-driven, trust-building work that actually keeps a client in their case. Rooney Agramonte, a case manager at Voto & Cavalli, described the shift plainly: “Following up with clients was one of the most time-consuming things we did. The AI Care Coordinator is easing the pain. I think it's something we want to keep.” Rooney A. Agramonte, Case Manager, Voto & Cavalli, P.C. Why this protects more than time Fewer missed appointments and fewer treatment gaps mean a cleaner, more complete record by the time a case reaches demand. The firm moves from reactive, finding out about a problem after it happened, to proactive, catching it while there is still time to act. And it does that without another line on the payroll. body_text: View All News Michael Mahan Joins Modine as President, Commercial HVAC July 13, 2026 RACINE, Wis. , July 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Modine (NYSE: MOD), a diversified global leader in thermal management technology and solutions, announced today that Michael Mahan has joined the company as President of the Commercial HVAC (CHVAC) segment. In this role, Mr. Mahan will be responsible for leading the newly formed segment, which provides heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and heat transfer solutions for the commercial, industrial, and aerospace markets. "I'm excited to welcome Michael to Modine as the leader of our CHVAC segment," said Modine President and Chief Executive Officer, Neil D. Brinker. "His extensive background positioning businesses as industrial technology leaders aligns with our strategic objectives for the CHVAC segment, making him exceptionally well-suited to lead the organization to new levels of performance and growth." Before joining Schneider Electric, he held executive roles of increasing responsibility at former GE companies. title: Pine Park Health | Understanding the Flu Season: What Residents of Senior Living Communities Should Know
summary: As we enter fall and winter months, flu season reemerges. Given the heightened risk of older adults in senior living communities, it’s a good idea to be especially cautious during these months.
body_text: As we enter fall and winter months, flu season reemerges. Each year, the CDC highlights that millions of people in the U.S. are afflicted by the flu, with older adults often being more susceptible . Given the heightened risk of older adults in senior living communities, it’s a good idea to be especially cautious during these months. Fortunately, there are a few steps you can take to bolster your defenses against the flu. What to Expect During Flu Season The flu is a rapidly spreading respiratory virus with sudden onset. After exposure, signs like body pains, fever, and coughing usually appear within one to four days and can persist for several days up to two weeks. When infected with the flu, individuals may experience some or all of these symptoms : fever* or feeling feverish/chills cough sore throat runny or stuffy nose muscle or body aches headaches fatigue (tiredness) *It’s important to note that not everyone with the flu will have a fever. If you're experiencing any of the above symptoms or have health concerns related to the flu or any other conditions, contact your primary care provider and community health staff. Timely intervention can prevent complications and increase chances of a swift recovery. Specialized Vaccines for Older Adults Similar to previous years, the CDC has highlighted the particular vulnerability of adults 65 and older during the flu season . This is because our bodies undergo several changes with age, and one such significant change pertains to the immune system. It might not respond as well to standard vaccinations as in younger individuals. Therefore, the high-dose and adjuvanted flu vaccines are designed to offer enhanced protection , countering the age-induced immune shifts. The primary flu vaccine options include: Fluzone High-Dose Quadrivalent : Designed for those 65 and above, this inactivated vaccine has an antigen concentration four times higher than standard vaccines. Fluad Quadrivalent : Another option for the 65 and older group, it's enriched with an adjuvant to boost the immune response. Flublok Quadrivalent : For those 18 and up, this unique vaccine is categorized as a recombinant protein vaccine. While you're arranging for your flu vaccine, consider verifying if you qualify for the new COVID-19 booster. Additionally, you might qualify for the latest RSV vaccination. Staying Healthy and Safe in Your Community Senior living communities offer lots of benefits, from social interactions to specialized care. However, shared spaces and group activities in any environment can lead to increased exposure to pathogens, including the flu virus. In addition to getting vaccinated, here are some tips specifically for adults in senior living communities to minimize their risk of contracting the flu and other respiratory illnesses: Practice Good Hand Hygiene: Regularly wash your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. If soap and water aren’t available, use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer. Maintain Distance: During peak flu season, consider keeping a safe distance from others, especially from those showing symptoms. Wear a Mask: In areas where there's a higher risk of transmission, wearing a mask can provide an added layer of protection. Eat Healthily and Stay Hydrated: A strong immune system can help fend off infections better. Consume a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals, and drink plenty of water. Limit Visitors: If possible, limit visitors during the peak flu season, especially those who might be sick or have been exposed to sick individuals. Stay Informed: Regularly communicate with community health staff or administrators about any potential flu outbreaks and follow their guidelines and recommendations. Promptly Report Symptoms: If you or a neighbor starts feeling unwell, report the symptoms immediately. Early detection and treatment can reduce the severity and spread of the flu. Throughout the flu season, it’s also important to stay in touch with your primary care team. Whether you’re a Pine Park Health patient or have another primary care provider, your care team should guide you on preventive measures and offer you personalized advice for your specific health needs and conditions. Regular check-ins, promptly addressing concerns, and actively seeking their recommendations can make all the difference in navigating this flu season.

title: Leaving Public School for a Microschool? What to Know Before You Switch
summary: Considering a microschool after public school? Here is what changes day to day, plus honest answers on socialization, grades, college, and transferring back.
body_text: If you’re weighing whether a microschool might be a better fit than your child’s public school, you probably have practical questions about what would actually change day to day, and whether a smaller, more personal setting can give your child what their current school hasn’t. At KaiPod Learning, we work with 150+ microschool founders across 30+ states, and these are the questions families bring to us most often when they’re exploring a change. Before we go further, it’s worth noting that microschools don’t all look the same. A microschool can operate as a private school, a homeschool-based learning center, or a network-affiliated school, and the daily experience varies from one to the next. So treat the descriptions below as the common patterns we see, then ask the specific school you’re considering how it does things. In this article: What changes when you move from public school to a microschool Common questions families have before making the switch Will my child have enough socialization? What about grades? How is student progress measured? Are microschools accredited? Will colleges take a microschool seriously? Can my child transfer back to public school later? Will my child fall behind academically? Questions to ask a microschool before enrolling Take the next step with confidence You May Be Interested In What changes when you move from public school to a microschool Most families notice three shifts right away, and together they explain why the day feels different for a child coming from a larger public school. The first is group size. Microschools are generally small, often around 10 to 15 students. In the microschools we work with, that size lets educators get to know each student more deeply, including their strengths, the subjects they find harder, and how they tend to work. Nationally, microschools serve an estimated 1 to 2 million students , and small group size is the through-line across nearly all of them. The second is more personalized learning. Students may not all work on the same lesson at the same pace. Learning is often adjusted to where a child is ready, with more room to master a topic before moving on rather than following a fixed calendar. For a child who was waiting for the class to catch up, or working hard to keep up, this is usually the most noticeable change. The third is a different daily structure. Schedules and routines tend to be more flexible, with project-based learning and more time for discussion and collaboration in a small group. You can read more about how microschools work if you want a fuller picture of a typical day. Common questions families have before making the switch Underneath the logistics, most families are carrying a few quieter questions. Is this a legitimate option? Will my child be taken seriously later? Can we change course if it doesn’t work out? Here are honest answers to the ones that come up most. Will my child have enough socialization? Smaller doesn’t mean isolated. Mixed-age grouping is common in microschools, so students interact across ages rather than only within a single grade. Many microschools also build in enrichment such as field trips, clubs, sports, and local activities, which widens a child’s social world beyond the classroom. Families in our network often tell us their children form closer friendships in a microschool, in part because a smaller group means students get to know each other more personally. If socialization is a top concern, ask the school you’re considering how it builds friendships, handles conflict, and creates time for students to connect. What about grades? Practices vary from school to school. Some microschools use traditional letter grades, some use narrative feedback, some use mastery-based assessment, and some use portfolios or demonstrations of learning. Students generally don’t take the same standardized tests they would in a public school. In our experience, families often end up with more detailed information about their child’s progress than a traditional report card provides, just in a different format. How is student progress measured? A microschool may start by giving your child a benchmark assessment, such as NWEA’s MAP Growth , to establish where they stand in math and reading. From there, many microschools track progress through a mix of portfolio reviews, projects, presentations, mastery tracking, and individual learning goals set with your child. The specifics differ by school, so we encourage you to ask exactly which assessments a school uses and how it reports results back to you. Are microschools accredited? Some are, and many aren’t. Accreditation is a formal review in which an outside organization evaluates whether a school meets certain standards. Many microschools don’t pursue traditional accreditation, often because the model is new, the process takes time and money, and accreditation frameworks were built for larger, more traditional schools. That choice isn’t a quality signal in either direction. Some microschools do pursue it, and some operate within a network that offers a pathway to accreditation. How much accreditation matters depends a lot on your child’s situation: When accreditation may matter more When accreditation may matter less Your child is in middle or high school and will need transcripts Your child is younger You anticipate moving between states or school systems You are prioritizing fit, relationships, and the daily learning experience A specific ESA or public funding program requires it The school provides clear documentation of learning progress Either way, what matters most is whether learning is well documented and whether the school can support your child’s next steps. For the full picture, see our article on whether microschools are accredited . Will colleges take a microschool seriously? This question comes up most with middle and high school families, and it’s a reasonable one to ask. Students from non-traditional settings, including homeschooling and microschools, are admitted to colleges. Admissions offices routinely review more than a standard transcript. They look at coursework, course descriptions, recommendations, portfolios, and a student’s achievements. Many colleges already publish clear processes for applicants from non-traditional backgrounds. The practical takeaway is to ask a microschool how it handles transcripts, course descriptions, and college counseling, especially during the high school years. Can my child transfer back to public school later? Generally, yes. Most districts have a process for placing transfer students regardless of where they were previously enrolled, and returning to public school is usually possible. The part that takes more attention is grade placement and, in the upper grades, high school credit, both of which can depend on your district and may rely on records or assessments. A few questions make a future transition smoother. Ask any microschool you’re considering: How do you document learning, and what records do families receive? Do you use benchmark assessments like MAP Growth that public schools recognize for grade-level placement? How do you handle transcripts for older students who may need them for high school credit or college applications? If you’re weighing the broader decision to move schools, our roadmap for families on switching schools walks through it in more detail. Will my child fall behind academically? A less traditional environment doesn’t mean less rigor. A strong microschool still sets clear learning goals and holds students accountable for meeting them. Many families come to a microschool precisely because their child’s needs weren’t being met in a larger setting, and the smaller environment is what helps them get back on track. When assessing rigor, you’ll want to look for a real curriculum, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, and solid documentation of progress. Questions to ask a microschool before enrolling Because microschools differ so much, the most useful thing you can do is ask each school directly how it operates. A short list to bring to a tour or first conversation: What does a typical day look like? How do you measure student progress? How do students socialize and build friendships? Do you issue grades or transcripts? Are you accredited, and if not, how do you document learning? How do you support students with different learning needs? Clear, specific answers tell you more about a school than any single label does. A microschool is one of several options families consider when they want a more personal setting, and whether it’s the right fit depends on what you’re looking for. If you want to see what’s available near you, you can find a microschool on our map. Take the next step with confidence Choosing a school is a significant decision, and you don’t have to make it without good information. The 2026 Family Guide to Microschools includes tools, checklists, and worksheets to help you evaluate schools, compare your options, and plan a smooth transition for your child.
